titre: Robinson Crusoe's Island Is Not the One in the Novel
accroche: An island off Chile has borne the name of Robinson Crusoe since 1966. In Defoe's novel, the island lies at the mouth of the Orinoco.
contenu_vulgarise:
From Santiago, Chile, a flight of a little under three hours leads to Robinson Crusoe Island, 670 kilometers from the coast, in the Pacific. Yet the name is recent, and the island is not the one in the book.

## A Name Given in 1966

Until January 1, 1966, the island was called Más a Tierra. On that day, Chilean president Eduardo Frei Montalva renamed it after the novel's hero, to attract tourists. The largest island of the Juan Fernández archipelago, Más Afuera, became Alejandro Selkirk Island at the same time.

## The Sailor

Alexander Selkirk, a Scot, was sailing master aboard the *Cinque Ports*, a privateer ship. In September 1704, after a dispute with his captain, Thomas Stradling, and judging the ship to be in poor condition, he asked to be left on Más a Tierra. He regretted it at once, but Stradling refused to take him back. The ship would later sink off Colombia.

On February 2, 1709, the privateer Woodes Rogers, aboard the *Duke*, found on the island a man “cloth'd in Goat-Skins, who look'd wilder than the first Owners of them.” Selkirk had spent four years and four months there. He told Rogers that he was born in Largo, in the county of Fife, and that Spaniards who had come ashore during his stay had chased him through the woods: he escaped them by climbing to the top of a tree. Rogers published his account in 1712.

## The Novel

Daniel Defoe published *Robinson Crusoe* in 1719. Selkirk is one of the models generally cited for the hero. But the text leaves no doubt about the geography: Crusoe understands, long after his shipwreck, that his island lies “in the mouth or gulf” of the great Orinoco River, and that the land he sees to the west is the large island of Trinidad. That places the novel in the Caribbean, about 4,300 kilometers from Juan Fernández.

## What the Name Displaced

The 1966 renaming therefore pasted a novel's title onto an island that, according to the novel itself, is not its own. It also named Alejandro Selkirk the island the sailor probably never saw: it lies 180 kilometers from the one where he lived.

Visitors today thus arrive on an island named after a fiction to look for the trace of a real man. What name, then, suits an island that owes its fame to a sailor and its name to a character?

carte.punch: The Chilean island renamed Robinson Crusoe in 1966 is not the island of Defoe's novel.
carte.idee: In Defoe's novel (1719), Crusoe's island lies at the mouth of the Orinoco, in the Caribbean. The Pacific island where Alexander Selkirk lived from 1704 to 1709 has borne the name of Robinson Crusoe only since January 1, 1966.

quiz.question: Why can the Chilean island renamed in 1966 not be the one in Defoe's novel?
choix: Because the novel places Crusoe's island at the mouth of the Orinoco
Because Selkirk lived on Más Afuera, the large neighboring island
Because Defoe sets his story in the Pacific Ocean, off California
Because Chile renamed it before the novel was published
quiz.explication: Crusoe understands that his island lies in the gulf of the Orinoco, near Trinidad: that is the Caribbean Sea, about 4,300 km from Juan Fernández. Selkirk did live on Más a Tierra, in the South Pacific; the renaming dates from 1966, long after the novel, and Defoe does not set his story in the Pacific, let alone off California.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Why does Alexander Selkirk find himself alone on Más a Tierra in 1704?
choix: He is abandoned by his crew after a mutiny
He asks to be put ashore after a dispute with his captain
His ship is wrecked on the island during a storm
He deserts to escape legal proceedings in Scotland
quiz_supplementaire.explication: After a dispute with Captain Stradling, and judging the Cinque Ports to be in poor condition, Selkirk himself asks to be put ashore on the island, in September 1704.

quiz_supplementaire.question: How long does Alexander Selkirk spend on the island before being rescued?
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Woodes Rogers finds him on February 2, 1709: Selkirk had spent four years and four months on the island since being put ashore in September 1704.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Why does Chilean president Eduardo Frei Montalva rename Más a Tierra in 1966?
choix: To honor the memory of a Chilean sailor
Because a United Nations decree requires it
To mark the centenary of Defoe's death
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The renaming of January 1, 1966 explicitly aims to attract tourists, pasting the name of the novel's hero onto the island where the sailor lived.
